      url: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.01070
---

## Definition

**Input:** a fixed number $K\ge2$ of observed series $Y_{i,1},\ldots,Y_{i,n_i}$ in a real Hilbert space $H$, positive integer sample sizes $n_i$, total size $M=\sum_{i=1}^K n_i$, integer block lengths $1\le b_i\le n_i$, and a mode, moving or tapered. For tapered mode also supply an admissible window with positive block norm at each $b_i$. Put

$$\bar Y_i=\frac1{n_i}\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}Y_{i,t},\qquad \bar Y_P=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^K n_i\bar Y_i,\qquad R_{i,t}=Y_{i,t}-\bar Y_i.$$

For each series $i=1,\ldots,K$, let $N_i=n_i-b_i+1$ and $k_i=\lceil n_i/b_i\rceil$. For every candidate start $j=1,\ldots,N_i$ and position $r=1,\ldots,b_i$, define the following arrays. In moving mode set $A_{i,j,r}=R_{i,j+r-1}$. In tapered mode set $A_{i,j,r}=a_{b_i}w_{b_i}(r)R_{i,j+r-1}$, with $a_{b_i}$ and $w_{b_i}$ as in [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]]. For each $i=1,\ldots,K$ and $s=1,\ldots,k_i$, draw independent uniform starts $J_{i,s}\in\{1,\ldots,N_i\}$, using the index law of [[alg-overlapping-block-resampling]]. For each within-block position define

$$c_{i,r}=\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j=1}^{N_i}A_{i,j,r}.$$

**Output:** for each $i$, a pseudo-series $Y^*_{i,1},\ldots,Y^*_{i,n_i}$. In the order $s=1,\ldots,k_i$, retain the positions $r=1,\ldots,q_{i,s}$, where $q_{i,s}=\min\{b_i,n_i-(s-1)b_i\}$, and set

$$Y^*_{i,(s-1)b_i+r}=\bar Y_P+A_{i,J_{i,s},r}-c_{i,r}.$$

Thus a divisible sample uses $k_i$ complete blocks; otherwise only the first $n_i-b_i\lfloor n_i/b_i\rfloor$ positions of the final block are retained. This centers each resampled residual position by its own conditional average, then gives every pseudo-series the same pooled location $\bar Y_P$. All block starts are conditionally independent across blocks and across series.

## Remarks

The algorithm is a finite-sample null imposition. Its validity for a statistic requires additional process and block-length hypotheses.

## Statement

For fixed data and either mode of [[alg-k-sample-null-constrained-block-bootstrap]], every pseudo-observation in every series has conditional expectation $\bar Y_P$. Consequently, for each $i$,

$$E^*\bar Y_i^*=\bar Y_P,$$

so the conditional mean functions of the $K$ pseudo-series are equal.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The fixed observed series, the block lengths and the independent uniform block-index randomization in the Statement.

[F1] [[alg-k-sample-null-constrained-block-bootstrap]]: At each series $i$ and within-block position $r$, the algorithm subtracts $c_{i,r}=N_i^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{N_i}A_{i,j,r}$ from a uniformly selected $A_{i,J_{i,s},r}$, then adds the same pooled mean $\bar Y_P$.

## Proof

**Given:** The data and pseudo-series construction in the Statement.

1.1 Fix $i,s,r$. Uniformity of $J_{i,s}$ gives $E^*A_{i,J_{i,s},r}-c_{i,r}=\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j=1}^{N_i}A_{i,j,r}-c_{i,r}=0$. Therefore $E^*Y^*_{i,(s-1)b_i+r}=\bar Y_P$, including positions in a truncated final block. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 The bootstrap mean $\bar Y_i^*$ is the average of exactly $n_i$ such pseudo-observations. Linearity of the finite conditional expectation gives $E^*\bar Y_i^*=\bar Y_P$ for every $i$. The common conditional mean proves the stated null imposition. [step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H=L^2([0,1])$, and let $(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a centered causal Bernoulli shift that is $L^2$-$m$-approximable under [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]]. Write

$$\delta_m=\bigl(E\|X_0-X_{0,m}\|_H^2\bigr)^{1/2}.$$

Retain the displayed source approximation condition $m\delta_m\to0$. For each $n$, let $b_n$ be an integer with $b_n\to\infty$ and $b_n/\sqrt n\to0$. For all sufficiently large $n$, these conditions give $1\le b_n\le n$; apply [[alg-moving-block-bootstrap]] to $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ on this admissible tail. All limits below concern that tail. Let $\Gamma$ be the long-run covariance operator from [[thm-hilbert-valued-clt-for-l2-m-approximable-bernoulli-shifts]], and let $\bar X_n^*=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nX_t^*$. Then

$$\mathcal L^*\!\left(\sqrt n(\bar X_n^*-E^*\bar X_n^*)\right)\Rightarrow\mathcal L(G)\quad\hbox{in probability},$$

and

$$\left\|n\,\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar X_n^*)-\Gamma\right\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{in probability},$$

where $G$ is the centered $H$-valued Gaussian with covariance $\Gamma$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the centered causal shift, summable replacement errors with $m\delta_m\to0$, and $b=b_n\to\infty$, $b/\sqrt n\to0$.

[F1] [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]] supplies the centered measurable causal representation, second moment, replacement extension and summable errors.

[F2] [[thm-hilbert-valued-clt-for-l2-m-approximable-bernoulli-shifts]] supplies the sampling-law limit $n^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^nX_t\Rightarrow G$ and its long-run covariance $\Gamma$. This is a sample-sum CLT, not a time-indexed FCLT.

[F3] [[alg-moving-block-bootstrap]] concatenates independent uniformly chosen overlapping blocks and retains exactly $n$ observations. [[lem-moving-block-bootstrap-conditional-covariance]] gives its exact full-plus-partial-block covariance formula.

[F4] [[lem-weighted-overlapping-block-moment-and-covariance-limits]] proves uniform integrability and empirical block covariance consistency for bounded normalized deterministic weights with fixed-lag autocorrelations tending to one. [[lem-conditional-independent-block-bootstrap-clt]] proves the conditional CLT, tightness and trace-norm covariance limit for exactly this resampling, including the last partial block.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is assumed. Its uses are those of the Hilbert sampling and conditional-block suppliers, including the complete orthonormal basis in the latter; no further choice principle is added here.

## Proof

**Given:** The assumptions and suppliers above.

1.1 Take $c_{b,\ell}=1$ for $1\le\ell\le b$. These weights are bounded by one, have $b^{-1}\sum_\ell c_{b,\ell}^2=1$, and for each fixed $h\ge0$ have $b^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{b-h}c_{b,\ell}c_{b,\ell+h}=(1-h/b)_+\to1$. Thus every process and weight hypothesis of [F4] holds, with exactly the displayed approximation rate and block regime. [given, F1, F4, A1, algebra]

2.1 Write $n=kb+r$, $0\le r<b$. Subtracting the conditional mean from the sum of the $k$ complete sampled blocks and the sampled length-$r$ prefix gives exactly the variable $Z_n^*$ in the conditional-block supplier. The candidate starts for both block sizes are the same $N=n-b+1$ starts, as required by [F3]. Hence [F4] gives the asserted conditional law and trace-norm covariance convergence. The Hilbert-Schmidt conclusion follows from $\|T\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\|T\|_1$; the covariance in question is exactly $n\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar X_n^*)$ by [F3]. The remainder has expected conditional squared norm $O(b/n)$, so no divisibility condition is used. [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The limiting Gaussian is the same $G$ as in the sampling-law limit [F2], because both have covariance $\Gamma$. This proves both stated limits with the approved hypotheses. [F2, F4, step 2.1] ∎

Under the independent-tail replacement convention in the process definition, [[lem-independent-tail-replacement-errors-are-monotone]] proves that summability already implies $m\delta_m\to0$. The displayed rate is retained to match the source theorem contract; it is not a stronger process restriction under this convention.

citations.quote:
Let $\mathcal B$ be the Borel sigma-algebra of $[0,1]$, generated by intervals with rational endpoints; let $dt$ be Lebesgue measure restricted to $\mathcal B$, and set $H=L^2([0,1],\mathcal B,dt;\mathbb R)$, with inner product $\langle x,y\rangle_H=\int_0^1x(u)y(u)\,du$. We use the quotient-by-null-functions convention for $L^2$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). The measure space is finite and countably generated, so under Countable Choice $H$ is separable ([[thm-l-p-of-a-sigma-finite-countably-generated-measure-space-is-separable]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-separable-space]]); [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]] verifies that this real pairing makes the quotient a Hilbert space.

Let $(S,\mathcal S,\nu)$ be a probability space and $(\delta_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ an independent identically distributed family of $S$-valued random elements with law $\nu$ ([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]], [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]], [[def-independent-random-elements]]). A **causal Bernoulli shift** with innovation law $\nu$ is a process
$$X_t=f(\delta_t,\delta_{t-1},\delta_{t-2},\ldots),\qquad t\in\mathbb Z,$$
where $f:S^{\mathbb N_0}\to H$ is measurable from the product sigma-algebra $\mathcal S^{\otimes\mathbb N_0}$ to the Borel sigma-algebra of $H$. This product-measurability formulation is meaningful for a merely measurable innovation space $S$.

On an independent product extension, take replacement innovations $\delta'_{t,m,k}$, indexed by $t\in\mathbb Z$, $m\in\mathbb N_0$, and integers $k\le t-m$, all with law $\nu$, mutually independent, and independent of the original innovations. Such a countable family and its product with the original probability space exist under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[cor-countable-independent-copies-exist]], [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]]). For $m\ge1$ define
$$X_{t,m}=f(\delta_t,\ldots,\delta_{t-m+1},\delta'_{t,m,t-m},\delta'_{t,m,t-m-1},\ldots),$$
and define the full replacement $X_{t,0}=f(\delta'_{t,0,t},\delta'_{t,0,t-1},\ldots)$. Each $X_{t,m}$ has the same marginal law as $X_t$; for fixed $m\ge1$ the sequence $(X_{t,m})_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is strictly stationary and $m$-dependent because its original-innovation windows have length $m$ and its replacement arrays are independent across $t$.

For every fixed $m\ge0$, the joint process $(X_t,X_{t,m})_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is strictly stationary: shifting all indices relabels a family of mutually independent innovations with the same law and commutes with the defining measurable maps. Consequently $D_{t,m}:=X_t-X_{t,m}$ is stationary and $\|D_{t,m}\|_{L^2(H)}=\delta_m$ for every $t$.

Write $\|X\|_{L^2(H)}=(\mathbb E\|X\|_H^2)^{1/2}$ and
$$\delta_m=\|X_0-X_{0,m}\|_{L^2(H)},\qquad m\ge0.$$
The process is **$L^2$-$m$-approximable** when
$$\mathbb E\|X_0\|_H^2<\infty\qquad\hbox{and}\qquad\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_m<\infty.$$
The same marginal law gives $\delta_0\le2\|X_0\|_{L^2(H)}<\infty$. For a Bochner-integrable $H$-valued random element $Y$, write $\mathbb E_B Y=\int Y\,d\mathbb P$; the moment condition makes $X_t$ and every $X_{t,m}$ Bochner integrable ([[def-bochner-integrable-function]], [[thm-bochner-integrability-criterion]]).

Here **strict stationarity** means invariance of every finite-dimensional law under integer shifts. A process is **$m$-dependent** if, for every $a\in\mathbb Z$, the sigma-algebras generated by $(X_s)_{s\le a}$ and $(X_s)_{s\ge a+m+1}$ are independent ([[def-independent-sigma-algebras-and-events]]). The stated input windows for $X_{t,m}$ are disjoint across these two index ranges, so they satisfy this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H=L^2([0,1],dt;\mathbb R)$ and let
$(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a centered, $L^2$-$m$-approximable causal
Bernoulli shift as defined in
[[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]], with Bochner mean
$\mathbb E_BX_0=0$. Let $\Gamma$ be its long-run covariance operator from
[[lem-long-run-covariance-is-trace-class]], and let $G$ be a centered
$H$-valued Gaussian random element with covariance $\Gamma$, whose existence
is given by [[lem-positive-trace-class-covariance-defines-hilbert-gaussian]].
Then, for $S_n=\sum_{t=1}^nX_t$,
$$n^{-1/2}S_n\ \Rightarrow\ G$$
in the weak topology of Borel probability measures on $H$. The covariance
kernel is the $L^2([0,1]^2)$ equivalence class $c$ in the long-run covariance
lemma, and its integral operator is $T_c=\Gamma$. This is a CLT for the
$H$-valued sample sums; it is not a functional CLT for the time-indexed
partial-sum process.

**Input:** observations $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ in a real Hilbert space $H$, and $1\le b\le n$.

**Output:** a pseudo-series $X_1^*,\ldots,X_n^*$, generated by [[alg-overlapping-block-resampling]]: within each selected block retain the original order and concatenate blocks in their draw order, truncating only the last block when $b\nmid n$. The conditional bootstrap sample mean is $\bar X_n^*=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nX_t^*$. Its conditional center is $E^*\bar X_n^*$, where $E^*$ averages over the independent uniform block starts while the observations remain fixed.

This algorithm specifies the resampling law only. It does not assert that the conditional law approximates the sampling law for any data-generating process or block-length regime.

For a dependent time series, each selected length-$b$ run is treated as a predeclared group of consecutive unit records under [[def-resampling-sampling-unit-contract]]; the group is resampled intact and its within-block order is preserved. This is the sampling-unit interface, not a bootstrap-validity result.

Fix $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in H$ and $1\le b\le n$. Put $N=n-b+1$, $k=\lfloor n/b\rfloor$, and $r=n-kb$. For $q\in\{b\}$, and also $q=r$ when $r>0$, define

$$S_j^{(q)}=\sum_{\ell=1}^q x_{j+\ell-1},\qquad \bar S_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N S_j^{(q)},\qquad C_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N(S_j^{(q)}-\bar S_q)\otimes(S_j^{(q)}-\bar S_q).$$

Set $C_0=0$. If $\bar X_n^*$ is the mean produced by [[alg-moving-block-bootstrap]], then its conditional covariance operator is

$$n\,\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar X_n^*)=\frac{kC_b+C_r}{n},$$

where the $C_r$ term is zero when $r=0$. Here $\operatorname{Cov}^*(Z)=E^*[(Z-E^*Z)\otimes(Z-E^*Z)]$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a centered $L^2$-$m$-approximable causal Bernoulli shift in $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R)$ under [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]], and suppose additionally that $m\delta_m\to0$. Put $\sigma=\|X_0\|_{L^2(H)}$, let $\Gamma$ be its long-run covariance operator, and put

$$K=\sigma^2+2\sigma\sum_{h\ge1}\delta_h.$$

For every integer $b\ge1$, let $c_{b,1},\ldots,c_{b,b}$ be deterministic real weights, uniformly bounded in absolute value by $A<\infty$. Define

$$Z_{j,b}=b^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell=1}^b c_{b,\ell}X_{j+\ell-1}.$$

Then $\{\|Z_{j,b}\|_H^2:j\in\mathbb Z,b\ge1\}$ is uniformly integrable, and for $0\le q\le b$,

$$E\left\|\sum_{\ell=1}^q c_{b,\ell}X_{j+\ell-1}\right\|_H^2\le A^2Kq.$$

If $P$ is any finite-rank orthogonal projection, $R=I-P$ and $\alpha_P=\|RX_0\|_{L^2(H)}$, then also

$$E\left\|\sum_{\ell=1}^q c_{b,\ell}RX_{j+\ell-1}\right\|_H^2\le A^2q\left(\alpha_P^2+2\alpha_P\sum_{h\ge1}\delta_h\right).$$

For $n\ge b$, set $N=n-b+1$ and $\bar Z_{n,b}=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NZ_{j,b}$. Then

$$E\|\bar Z_{n,b}\|_H^2\le A^2Kb/N.$$

Suppose further that $b=b_n\to\infty$, $b_n/n\to0$, and the weights satisfy

$$b^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^bc_{b,\ell}^2=1,\qquad q_b(h):=b^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{b-h}c_{b,\ell}c_{b,\ell+h}\longrightarrow1\quad\text{for every fixed }h\ge0.$$

The centered overlapping-block covariance then satisfies the stronger $L^1$ trace-norm limit

$$E\left\|N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N(Z_{j,b}-\bar Z_{n,b})\otimes(Z_{j,b}-\bar Z_{n,b})-\Gamma\right\|_1\longrightarrow0.$$

In particular it converges in probability in trace norm. Both the MBB weights $c_{b,\ell}=1$ and the actual TBB weights $c_{b,\ell}=a_bw((\ell-\tfrac12)/b)$ satisfy these weight hypotheses for all sufficiently large $b$. For any complete finite or countable orthonormal basis and its initial-coordinate projections $P_d$, the projection-tail coefficient $\alpha_{P_d}^2+2\alpha_{P_d}\sum_{h\ge1}\delta_h$ tends to zero as $d\to\infty$.

Assume AC and all the process and weight hypotheses of [[lem-weighted-overlapping-block-moment-and-covariance-limits]], including squared normalization and convergence of each fixed-lag weight autocorrelation to one. Let $b=b_n\to\infty$ with $b/\sqrt n\to0$, $N=n-b+1$, $k=\lfloor n/b\rfloor$, $r=n-kb$, and

$$B_{j,q}=\sum_{\ell=1}^q c_{b,\ell}X_{j+\ell-1},\qquad \bar B_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NB_{j,q},\qquad C_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N(B_{j,q}-\bar B_q)\otimes(B_{j,q}-\bar B_q),$$

with $B_{j,0}=\bar B_0=C_0=0$. Conditional on the observations choose independent uniform starts $J_1,\ldots,J_{k+1}$ in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and set

$$Z_n^*=n^{-1/2}\left\{\sum_{s=1}^k(B_{J_s,b}-\bar B_b)+(B_{J_{k+1},r}-\bar B_r)\right\}.$$

Then, for the centered Hilbert Gaussian $G$ of covariance $\Gamma$,

$$\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)\Rightarrow\mathcal L(G)\quad\hbox{in probability},\qquad \left\|\operatorname{Cov}^*(Z_n^*)-\Gamma\right\|_1\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$

Trace-norm convergence implies convergence in Hilbert-Schmidt norm as well. The conditional laws are tight in probability: for every $\varepsilon,\eta>0$ there is a deterministic compact $K\subset H$ such that $\limsup_nP\{P^*(Z_n^*\notin K)>\varepsilon\}<\eta$. The complete blocks satisfy conditional Lindeberg, and the final partial block has $E E^*\|n^{-1/2}(B_{J_{k+1},r}-\bar B_r)\|^2=O(b/n)$. Replacing every $X_t$ by $X_t-M_n$ for any common data-dependent $M_n\in H$ leaves $Z_n^*$ and all its conditional covariances unchanged.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H=L^2([0,1])$, and let $(Y_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a centered causal Bernoulli shift that is $L^2$-$m$-approximable under [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]]. Write

$$\delta_m=\bigl(E\|Y_0-Y_{0,m}\|_H^2\bigr)^{1/2}.$$

Assume $m\delta_m\to0$, and let the integers $b_n\to\infty$ with $b_n/\sqrt n\to0$. Let the taper satisfy the support, positivity-near-$1/2$, symmetry and monotonicity conditions in [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]]. For all sufficiently large $n$, $1\le b_n\le n$ and $W_{b_n}>0$, the latter by [[lem-taper-window-l2-normalization]]. Apply that algorithm to $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ only on this admissible tail; all limits below concern that tail. Write $\bar Y_n^*=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_t^*$ for the resulting bootstrap mean. Let $\Gamma$ be the long-run covariance operator from [[thm-hilbert-valued-clt-for-l2-m-approximable-bernoulli-shifts]]. Then

$$\mathcal L^*\!\left(\sqrt n(\bar Y_n^*-E^*\bar Y_n^*)\right)\Rightarrow\mathcal L(G)\quad\hbox{in probability},$$

and

$$\left\|n\,\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar Y_n^*)-\Gamma\right\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{in probability},$$

where $G$ is centered Gaussian with covariance $\Gamma$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC; the centered causal shift, summable replacement errors with $m\delta_m\to0$; the stated block regime; and the admissible taper.

[F1] [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]] supplies the measurable causal representation, second moment and summable replacement errors.

[F2] [[thm-hilbert-valued-clt-for-l2-m-approximable-bernoulli-shifts]] supplies the sampling-law limit and centered Gaussian $G$ of covariance $\Gamma$; it makes no time-indexed FCLT assertion.

[F3] [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]] uses midpoint weights $c_{b,\ell}=a_bw((\ell-1/2)/b)$ on sample-centered observations, independent uniform starts and truncation to exactly $n$ observations. [[lem-tapered-block-bootstrap-conditional-covariance]] gives the exact conditional full-plus-partial covariance.

[F4] [[lem-taper-window-l2-normalization]] gives $W_b^2/b\to I_w>0$, so $a_b=\sqrt b/W_b$ is defined and bounded for all sufficiently large $b$.

[F5] [[lem-weighted-overlapping-block-moment-and-covariance-limits]] proves uniform integrability and empirical trace-norm covariance consistency for bounded normalized weights with fixed-lag autocorrelations tending to one. [[lem-conditional-independent-block-bootstrap-clt]] proves the corresponding conditional law, tightness, trace-norm covariance limit and partial-block bound; subtracting any common sample center leaves its centered blocks unchanged.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is assumed. Its uses are inherited from the sampling and conditional-block suppliers, including the latter's complete orthonormal basis; no further choice principle is added.

## Proof

**Given:** The assumptions and suppliers above.

1.1 Set $c_{b,\ell}=a_bw((\ell-1/2)/b)$ and extend this finite sequence by zero on all other integer indices. The exact normalization gives $b^{-1}\sum_\ell c_{b,\ell}^2=1$, and [F4] bounds its maximum by a constant $A$ for sufficiently large $b$. Symmetry and monotonicity of $w$ make the sequence nonnegative and unimodal, including the possible equal central pair; hence its discrete total variation, including both exterior zero tails, is at most $2A$. For every fixed integer $h\ge1$, telescoping $h$ successive shifts gives $\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}|c_{b,\ell+h}-c_{b,\ell}|\le2Ah$. Therefore
$$\left|b^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{b-h}c_{b,\ell}c_{b,\ell+h}-1\right|\le\frac{A}{b}\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}|c_{b,\ell+h}-c_{b,\ell}|\le\frac{2A^2h}{b}\longrightarrow0.$$
This verifies every weight hypothesis of [F5], even for discontinuous monotone tapers. The process hypotheses and displayed rate are exactly [F1] and the Given. [given, F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, algebra]

2.1 For each full or partial weighted block, replacing $Y_t$ by $Y_t-\bar Y_n$ subtracts $(\sum_{\ell=1}^qc_{b,\ell})\bar Y_n$ from every candidate block with $q$ entries. Its empirical conditional center over the $N=n-b+1$ starts subtracts the same vector, so all conditionally centered block sums agree exactly with those formed from $Y_t$. Thus $\sqrt n(\bar Y_n^*-E^*\bar Y_n^*)$ is precisely $Z_n^*$ in [F5], with the full-taper prefix weights on its last $r=n-b\lfloor n/b\rfloor$ entries. [F3, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply [F5]. It gives conditional weak convergence to $G$, conditional tightness, and convergence of the exact covariance $n\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar Y_n^*)$ in trace norm, which implies its stated Hilbert-Schmidt convergence. The final prefix has expected conditional squared norm $O(b/n)$ and is negligible without requiring $b\mid n$. Its limiting covariance $\Gamma$ is the sampling target in [F2], completing both claims. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

Under the independent-tail replacement convention in the process definition, [[lem-independent-tail-replacement-errors-are-monotone]] proves that summability already implies $m\delta_m\to0$. The displayed rate is retained to match the source theorem contract; it is not a stronger process restriction under this convention.

Let $\mathcal B$ be the Borel sigma-algebra of $[0,1]$, generated by intervals with rational endpoints; let $dt$ be Lebesgue measure restricted to $\mathcal B$, and set $H=L^2([0,1],\mathcal B,dt;\mathbb R)$, with inner product $\langle x,y\rangle_H=\int_0^1x(u)y(u)\,du$. We use the quotient-by-null-functions convention for $L^2$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). The measure space is finite and countably generated, so under Countable Choice $H$ is separable ([[thm-l-p-of-a-sigma-finite-countably-generated-measure-space-is-separable]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-separable-space]]); [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]] verifies that this real pairing makes the quotient a Hilbert space.

Let $(S,\mathcal S,\nu)$ be a probability space and $(\delta_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ an independent identically distributed family of $S$-valued random elements with law $\nu$ ([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]], [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]], [[def-independent-random-elements]]). A **causal Bernoulli shift** with innovation law $\nu$ is a process
$$X_t=f(\delta_t,\delta_{t-1},\delta_{t-2},\ldots),\qquad t\in\mathbb Z,$$
where $f:S^{\mathbb N_0}\to H$ is measurable from the product sigma-algebra $\mathcal S^{\otimes\mathbb N_0}$ to the Borel sigma-algebra of $H$. This product-measurability formulation is meaningful for a merely measurable innovation space $S$.

On an independent product extension, take replacement innovations $\delta'_{t,m,k}$, indexed by $t\in\mathbb Z$, $m\in\mathbb N_0$, and integers $k\le t-m$, all with law $\nu$, mutually independent, and independent of the original innovations. Such a countable family and its product with the original probability space exist under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[cor-countable-independent-copies-exist]], [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]]). For $m\ge1$ define
$$X_{t,m}=f(\delta_t,\ldots,\delta_{t-m+1},\delta'_{t,m,t-m},\delta'_{t,m,t-m-1},\ldots),$$
and define the full replacement $X_{t,0}=f(\delta'_{t,0,t},\delta'_{t,0,t-1},\ldots)$. Each $X_{t,m}$ has the same marginal law as $X_t$; for fixed $m\ge1$ the sequence $(X_{t,m})_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is strictly stationary and $m$-dependent because its original-innovation windows have length $m$ and its replacement arrays are independent across $t$.

For every fixed $m\ge0$, the joint process $(X_t,X_{t,m})_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is strictly stationary: shifting all indices relabels a family of mutually independent innovations with the same law and commutes with the defining measurable maps. Consequently $D_{t,m}:=X_t-X_{t,m}$ is stationary and $\|D_{t,m}\|_{L^2(H)}=\delta_m$ for every $t$.

Write $\|X\|_{L^2(H)}=(\mathbb E\|X\|_H^2)^{1/2}$ and
$$\delta_m=\|X_0-X_{0,m}\|_{L^2(H)},\qquad m\ge0.$$
The process is **$L^2$-$m$-approximable** when
$$\mathbb E\|X_0\|_H^2<\infty\qquad\hbox{and}\qquad\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_m<\infty.$$
The same marginal law gives $\delta_0\le2\|X_0\|_{L^2(H)}<\infty$. For a Bochner-integrable $H$-valued random element $Y$, write $\mathbb E_B Y=\int Y\,d\mathbb P$; the moment condition makes $X_t$ and every $X_{t,m}$ Bochner integrable ([[def-bochner-integrable-function]], [[thm-bochner-integrability-criterion]]).

Here **strict stationarity** means invariance of every finite-dimensional law under integer shifts. A process is **$m$-dependent** if, for every $a\in\mathbb Z$, the sigma-algebras generated by $(X_s)_{s\le a}$ and $(X_s)_{s\ge a+m+1}$ are independent ([[def-independent-sigma-algebras-and-events]]). The stated input windows for $X_{t,m}$ are disjoint across these two index ranges, so they satisfy this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H=L^2([0,1],dt;\mathbb R)$ and let
$(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a centered, $L^2$-$m$-approximable causal
Bernoulli shift as defined in
[[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]], with Bochner mean
$\mathbb E_BX_0=0$. Let $\Gamma$ be its long-run covariance operator from
[[lem-long-run-covariance-is-trace-class]], and let $G$ be a centered
$H$-valued Gaussian random element with covariance $\Gamma$, whose existence
is given by [[lem-positive-trace-class-covariance-defines-hilbert-gaussian]].
Then, for $S_n=\sum_{t=1}^nX_t$,
$$n^{-1/2}S_n\ \Rightarrow\ G$$
in the weak topology of Borel probability measures on $H$. The covariance
kernel is the $L^2([0,1]^2)$ equivalence class $c$ in the long-run covariance
lemma, and its integral operator is $T_c=\Gamma$. This is a CLT for the
$H$-valued sample sums; it is not a functional CLT for the time-indexed
partial-sum process.

**Input:** observations $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ in a real Hilbert space $H$, an integer $1\le b\le n$, and a window $w:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ that vanishes off $[0,1]$, is positive on a neighbourhood of $1/2$, satisfies $w(1-u)=w(u)$, and is nondecreasing on $[0,1/2]$. Put $w_b(r)=w((r-\tfrac12)/b)$ for $1\le r\le b$, $W_b=(\sum_{r=1}^bw_b(r)^2)^{1/2}$, and $a_b=\sqrt b/W_b$. The procedure is admissible only when $W_b>0$.

**Center and taper:** set $\bar Y_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_t$ and $R_t=Y_t-\bar Y_n$. For each start $j\in\{1,\ldots,n-b+1\}$, form the block

$$\bigl(a_bw_b(1)R_j,\ldots,a_bw_b(b)R_{j+b-1}\bigr).$$

**Resample:** use the independent uniform block starts from [[alg-overlapping-block-resampling]], multiply each selected centered observation by its within-block taper and the factor $a_b$, concatenate in draw order, and retain the first $n$ entries. The conditional bootstrap mean is centered by its own conditional expectation when used to approximate the sampling law of $\sqrt n\,\bar Y_n$.

The factor $a_b$ compensates for the window's squared-weight sum in the block-sum variance calculation; this definition alone gives no bootstrap validity result.

For a dependent time series, the selected length-$b$ consecutive run is the resampling unit under [[def-resampling-sampling-unit-contract]]. The taper changes each unit record's within-block weight but the whole block is selected and resampled together; validity remains a separate theorem.

Fix $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\in H$, a block length $1\le b\le n$ with $W_b>0$, and the taper and scale $w_b,a_b$ from [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]]. Set $R_t=Y_t-\bar Y_n$, $N=n-b+1$, $k=\lfloor n/b\rfloor$, and $r=n-kb$. For $q=b$, and also $q=r$ when $r>0$, define the tapered partial block sum

$$T_j^{(q)}=a_b\sum_{\ell=1}^q w_b(\ell)R_{j+\ell-1},\qquad \bar T_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N T_j^{(q)},\qquad V_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N(T_j^{(q)}-\bar T_q)\otimes(T_j^{(q)}-\bar T_q).$$

Set $V_0=0$. If $\bar X_n^*$ is the tapered bootstrap mean, then

$$n\,\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar X_n^*)=\frac{kV_b+V_r}{n},$$

with the $V_r$ term zero when $r=0$.

Let $w$ satisfy the taper conditions in [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]]. As the positive integer $b\to\infty$, $w^2$ is Riemann integrable on $[0,1]$, and

$$\frac{1}{b}\sum_{j=1}^b w\!\left(\frac{j-\tfrac12}{b}\right)^2\longrightarrow I_w:=\int_0^1 w(u)^2\,du>0.$$

Consequently, $W_b>0$ for all sufficiently large $b$ and $a_b=\sqrt b/W_b\to I_w^{-1/2}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a centered $L^2$-$m$-approximable causal Bernoulli shift in $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R)$ under [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]], and suppose additionally that $m\delta_m\to0$. Put $\sigma=\|X_0\|_{L^2(H)}$, let $\Gamma$ be its long-run covariance operator, and put

$$K=\sigma^2+2\sigma\sum_{h\ge1}\delta_h.$$

For every integer $b\ge1$, let $c_{b,1},\ldots,c_{b,b}$ be deterministic real weights, uniformly bounded in absolute value by $A<\infty$. Define

$$Z_{j,b}=b^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell=1}^b c_{b,\ell}X_{j+\ell-1}.$$

Then $\{\|Z_{j,b}\|_H^2:j\in\mathbb Z,b\ge1\}$ is uniformly integrable, and for $0\le q\le b$,

$$X_t=f(\delta_t,\delta_{t-1},\delta_{t-2},\ldots),\qquad t\in\mathbb Z,$$

## Definition

Let $E$ be a separable complete metric space, let $\mathcal D_n$ be the sigma-algebra generated by the observed data at sample size $n$, and let $Z_n^*$ be a bootstrap random element whose remaining randomness is the resampling randomization. Write $\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)$ for its conditional Borel probability law given $\mathcal D_n$. Supply as part of the data a metric $d_w$ on Borel probability measures on $E$ such that $d_w(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$ exactly when $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$ in the sense of [[def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures]]. Assume the displayed metric distance is a measurable real random variable. For a fixed Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $E$, we say that $Z_n^*$ converges conditionally weakly in probability to $\mu$ when

$$d_w\!\left(\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*),\mu\right)\longrightarrow 0\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$

The metric is supplied as a hypothesis; this definition makes no metric-existence assertion. It applies to separable complete metric spaces, including separable Banach spaces, their closed linear subspaces and finite products.

## Remarks

The conditioning fixes the observations and averages only over bootstrap randomization. A conditional limit in probability is not an assertion of almost-sure conditional convergence.

## Statement

Let $E,F$ be separable Banach spaces, $E_0\subseteq E$ a closed linear subspace, $\theta\in E$, and $D\subseteq E$ a neighbourhood of $\theta$. Let $t_n>0$ decrease to zero, let $Z_n\in E_0$ be data-measurable and tight, and let $Z_n^*\in E_0$ be bootstrap random elements such that $\theta+t_nZ_n$ and $\theta+t_n(Z_n+Z_n^*)$ lie in $D$ with probability tending to one. Supply weak-convergence metrics on probability laws on $E_0$ and $F$ as in [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]], with measurable distances for the conditional laws below. Assume:

1. $\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)$ converges conditionally weakly in probability to the fixed law of $G\in E_0$, as in [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]];
2. $Z_n^*$ is conditionally tight in probability: for each $\epsilon,\eta>0$, there is a deterministic compact $K\subset E_0$ such that $\limsup_n\Pr\{\Pr^*(Z_n^*\notin K)>\epsilon\}<\eta$;
3. $D$ is Borel and $\Psi:D\to F$ is Borel measurable and Hadamard differentiable at $\theta$, tangentially to $E_0$, with continuous linear derivative $\Psi'_\theta$ as in [[def-hadamard-differentiability-tangentially]].

Then

$$\mathcal L^*\!\left(t_n^{-1}\{\Psi(\theta+t_n(Z_n+Z_n^*))-\Psi(\theta+t_nZ_n)\}\right)$$

converges conditionally weakly in probability to the law of $\Psi'_\theta(G)$. Define the displayed bootstrap difference to be $0\in F$ whenever either argument lies outside $D$; the assumed vanishing probability of this event makes this convention asymptotically immaterial.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The spaces, sequences, conditional convergence, conditional tightness, domain and differentiability assumptions in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-hadamard-differentiability-tangentially]]: Along every $t_m\to0$ and $h_m\to h\in E_0$, the difference quotient $\{\Psi(\theta+t_mh_m)-\Psi(\theta)\}/t_m$ converges to $\Psi'_\theta(h)$, where $\Psi'_\theta$ is continuous and linear.

[F2] [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]]: Conditional weak convergence means that a metric generating weak convergence between the conditional bootstrap law and the fixed limiting law tends to zero in probability.

[F3] [[thm-portmanteau-theorem]]: Weak convergence of Borel probabilities is equivalent to the closed-set upper bound $\limsup_n\mu_n(C)\le\mu(C)$ for every closed set $C$.

[F4] [[thm-continuous-mapping-theorem]]: If $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$ and a measurable map $g$ is continuous $\mu$-almost everywhere, then the image laws satisfy $g_*\mu_n\Rightarrow g_*\mu$.

[F5] [[thm-subsequence-characterization-of-convergence-in-probability]]: A scalar sequence tends to zero in probability exactly when every subsequence has a further subsequence tending to zero almost surely.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and facts in the Statement and Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 For every compact $K\subset E_0$, $\sup_{h\in K}\left\|t_n^{-1}\{\Psi(\theta+t_nh)-\Psi(\theta)\}-\Psi'_\theta(h)\right\|_F\longrightarrow0$. If this failed, some subsequence would have $h_n\in K$ with the displayed norm bounded below by a positive constant. Compactness gives a further subsequence $h_n\to h\in K$; [F1] applied to that subsequence makes the norm tend to zero, a contradiction. [F1, given, choose]

2.1 Write $T_n^*$ for the bootstrap difference with the stated convention, and $R_n^*=T_n^*-\Psi'_\theta(Z_n^*)$. Fix $\delta,\rho,\eta>0$. Tightness gives a compact $K_0$ with $\limsup_n\Pr(Z_n\notin K_0)<\eta$; conditional tightness gives compact $K_1$ with $\limsup_n\Pr\{\Pr^*(Z_n^*\notin K_1)>\rho/2\}<\eta$. Because $D$ is a neighbourhood of $\theta$, the arguments associated to the bounded compact sets $K_0$ and $K_0+K_1$ lie in $D$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Step 1.1 on these two compact sets and linearity show uniformly there that $\|R_n^*\|<\delta$. Since $Z_n$ is fixed under conditioning, $\Pr^*(\|R_n^*\|>\delta)\le\mathbf1_{\{Z_n\notin K_0\}}+\Pr^*(Z_n^*\notin K_1)$ eventually. Thus the limit superior of $\Pr\{\Pr^*(\|R_n^*\|>\delta)>\rho\}$ is at most $2\eta$. Letting $\eta\downarrow0$ proves $\Pr^*(\|R_n^*\|>\delta)\to0$ in probability for every $\delta>0$. [F1, given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Start with any subsequence. The nonnegative scalar $\min(1,d_w(\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*),\mathcal L(G)))+\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j}\Pr^*(\|R_n^*\|>1/j)$ tends to zero in probability: truncate the sum, use step 2.1 for its finitely many terms, and bound the tail by its geometric sum. By [F5], extract a further subsequence along which this scalar tends to zero almost surely, so the input metric distance and every remainder probability do also. Fix an outcome in their common probability-one event. The continuous mapping theorem [F4] gives weak convergence of the conditional laws of $\Psi'_\theta(Z_n^*)$. For every closed $C\subset F$ and $\delta>0$, $\Pr^*(T_n^*\in C)\le\Pr^*(\|R_n^*\|>\delta)+\Pr^*(\Psi'_\theta(Z_n^*)\in C^\delta)$, where $C^\delta=\{y:d(y,C)\le\delta\}$ is closed. Apply [F3] and let $\delta\downarrow0$; continuity from above of the fixed limiting probability gives the closed-set bound for $T_n^*$. Thus [F3] gives weak convergence on this outcome, hence convergence to zero of the supplied output weak-metric distance. A final application of [F5] proves convergence of that distance in probability along the full sequence. [F2, F3, F4, F5, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

This theorem is conditional on the bootstrap limit and tightness hypotheses. It does not prove those hypotheses for a particular resampling algorithm.

## Statement

Let $H$ be a real separable Hilbert space. Fix $K\ge2$. Let $Y_{i,1},\ldots,Y_{i,n_i}\in H$, $1\le i\le K$, be independent functional time-series samples, $M=\sum_i n_i\to\infty$, and suppose $n_i/M\to\theta_i\in(0,1)$. Under the null hypothesis $\mu_1=\cdots=\mu_K=\mu$, let $\bar Y_i$ be the sample means and let $\bar Y_P=M^{-1}\sum_i n_i\bar Y_i$. Apply [[alg-k-sample-null-constrained-block-bootstrap]] to these observations with integer block lengths $1\le b_i\le n_i$ for every sample size used and a specified moving or tapered mode. In tapered mode supply the admissible windows and strictly positive block norms required by [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]] at each $b_i$. Draw the starts conditionally independently across series and blocks, and write $\bar Y_i^*$ for the resulting pseudo-series means.

Assume the original centered mean vector

$$U_M=\bigl(\sqrt{n_i}(\bar Y_i-\mu)\bigr)_{i=1}^K$$

converges weakly to a joint law $\mathcal L(G_1,\ldots,G_K)$, and assume the conditional law of

$$U_M^*=\bigl(\sqrt{n_i}(\bar Y_i^*-\bar Y_P)\bigr)_{i=1}^K$$

converges conditionally weakly in probability to that same joint law and is conditionally tight in probability: for every $\epsilon,\eta>0$ there is a deterministic compact $C\subset H^K$ such that $\limsup_M\Pr\{\Pr^*(U_M^*\notin C)>\epsilon\}<\eta$. These are explicit joint-limit hypotheses; this theorem does not derive them from the MBB or TBB conditions.

Define the contrast maps

$$L_M(z_1,\ldots,z_K)=\bigl(\sqrt{M/n_i}\,z_i-\sqrt{M/n_K}\,z_K\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1},\qquad L_\theta(z)=\bigl(z_i/\sqrt{\theta_i}-z_K/\sqrt{\theta_K}\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1}.$$

For every continuous $\Psi:H^{K-1}\to S$ into a metric space $S$, the conditional law of $\Psi(L_MU_M^*)$ converges testwise in probability to the law of $\Psi(L_\theta(G_1,\ldots,G_K))$: for every bounded continuous $f:S\to\mathbb R$, the corresponding conditional expectation tends in probability to $E f(\Psi(L_\theta(G_1,\ldots,G_K)))$. If $S$ is separable and complete and a weak-convergence metric with measurable conditional distances is supplied, the conclusion is also conditional weak convergence in probability in the sense of [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]]. Under the null, the sampling law of $\Psi(L_MU_M)$ has the same limit. The maps may be squared norms, integrated linear contrasts, or any other continuous statistic of this scaled contrast.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The samples, null, sample-size proportions, joint sampling limit and joint conditional bootstrap limit in the Statement.

[F1] [[alg-k-sample-null-constrained-block-bootstrap]]: Every pseudo-series has conditional mean equal to the pooled sample mean $\bar Y_P$.

[F2] [[lem-k-sample-null-centering]]: For each $i$, $E^*\bar Y_i^*=\bar Y_P$.

[F3] [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]]: The conditional law converges in probability in a metric that generates weak convergence.

[F4] [[thm-continuous-mapping-theorem]]: Weak convergence is preserved by a measurable map whose discontinuity set has limiting probability zero; in particular this applies to continuous maps.

[F5] [[def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures]] gives convergence of bounded continuous test integrals. [[thm-continuity-from-above-for-measures]] gives vanishing tails of the finite random norm $\|G\|$; the radial-cutoff argument in step 2.1 uses no compact-tightness theorem or additional choice axiom.

[F6] [[thm-subsequence-characterization-of-convergence-in-probability]] gives the almost-sure further-subsequence criterion for scalar convergence in probability. [[thm-portmanteau-theorem]] gives the closed-set criterion for weak convergence.


## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses and facts in the Statement and Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 Since every pseudo-series has conditional mean $\bar Y_P$ by [F1]-[F2], that common location cancels in every contrast. 2.1 Endow the finite products with their Hilbert product norms. The coefficients in $L_M$ converge to those of $L_\theta$, hence $a_M=\|L_M-L_\theta\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0$. For $R>0$, the function $\chi_R(z)=\min\{1,\max\{0,\|z\|-R\}\}$ is bounded and continuous, vanishes when $\|z\|\le R$, and equals one when $\|z\|\ge R+1$. Thus [F5] and the given weak convergence imply
$$\limsup_M\Pr(\|U_M\|\ge R+1)\le E\chi_R(G)\le\Pr(\|G\|>R)\longrightarrow0\quad(R\to\infty).$$
The last limit follows from continuity from above since $G$ has finite norm. Given $\delta>0$, eventually $a_M(R+1)\le\delta$, so $\Pr(\|(L_M-L_\theta)U_M\|>\delta)\le\Pr(\|U_M\|>R+1)$. For the conditional discrepancy, every supplied compact $C\subset H^K$ is norm bounded, say by $R_C$. For arbitrary $\epsilon,\eta>0$, conditional tightness supplies such a $C$ with $\limsup_M\Pr\{\Pr^*(U_M^*\notin C)>\epsilon\}<\eta$. 2.2 By [F4], $L_\theta U_M\Rightarrow L_\theta G$. For a closed $B\subset H^{K-1}$, the sampling probability of $L_MU_M\in B$ is at most the discrepancy probability from step 2.1 plus $\Pr(L_\theta U_M\in B^\delta)$, where $B^\delta$ is the closed $\delta$-neighbourhood. 3.1 Apply [F4] to $\Psi$ for the sampling convergence and, on every almost-sure subsequence outcome of step 2.2, for conditional convergence. When the supplied output weak-convergence metric is available on separable complete $S$, the same outcome-wise weak convergence says its distance to the fixed limiting law tends to zero. For a statistic expressed as a differentiable functional of the unscaled mean vector, the conditional delta theorem [[thm-conditional-bootstrap-hadamard-delta-method]] supplies the required Hadamard-differentiability route. The single-series conditional CLTs and tightness bounds are supplied by [[thm-moving-block-bootstrap-clt-for-dependent-data]] and [[thm-tapered-block-bootstrap-clt-for-dependent-data]] under their respective hypotheses. This theorem retains its explicit joint-limit hypotheses; those hypotheses must be checked for the chosen independent-series and resampling construction.

manifest_row.statement:
Let $H$ be a real separable Hilbert space. Fix $K\ge2$. Let $Y_{i,1},\ldots,Y_{i,n_i}\in H$, $1\le i\le K$, be independent functional time-series samples, $M=\sum_i n_i\to\infty$, and suppose $n_i/M\to\theta_i\in(0,1)$. Under the null hypothesis $\mu_1=\cdots=\mu_K=\mu$, let $\bar Y_i$ be the sample means and let $\bar Y_P=M^{-1}\sum_i n_i\bar Y_i$. Apply [[alg-k-sample-null-constrained-block-bootstrap]] to these observations with integer block lengths $1\le b_i\le n_i$ for every sample size used and a specified moving or tapered mode. In tapered mode supply the admissible windows and strictly positive block norms required by [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]] at each $b_i$. Draw the starts conditionally independently across series and blocks, and write $\bar Y_i^*$ for the resulting pseudo-series means.

Assume the original centered mean vector

$$U_M=\bigl(\sqrt{n_i}(\bar Y_i-\mu)\bigr)_{i=1}^K$$

converges weakly to a joint law $\mathcal L(G_1,\ldots,G_K)$, and assume the conditional law of

$$U_M^*=\bigl(\sqrt{n_i}(\bar Y_i^*-\bar Y_P)\bigr)_{i=1}^K$$

converges conditionally weakly in probability to that same joint law and is conditionally tight in probability: for every $\epsilon,\eta>0$ there is a deterministic compact $C\subset H^K$ such that $\limsup_M\Pr\{\Pr^*(U_M^*\notin C)>\epsilon\}<\eta$. These are explicit joint-limit hypotheses; this theorem does not derive them from the MBB or TBB conditions.

Define the contrast maps

$$L_M(z_1,\ldots,z_K)=\bigl(\sqrt{M/n_i}\,z_i-\sqrt{M/n_K}\,z_K\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1},\qquad L_\theta(z)=\bigl(z_i/\sqrt{\theta_i}-z_K/\sqrt{\theta_K}\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1}.$$

For every continuous $\Psi:H^{K-1}\to S$ into a metric space $S$, the conditional law of $\Psi(L_MU_M^*)$ converges testwise in probability to the law of $\Psi(L_\theta(G_1,\ldots,G_K))$: for every bounded continuous $f:S\to\mathbb R$, the corresponding conditional expectation tends in probability to $E f(\Psi(L_\theta(G_1,\ldots,G_K)))$. If $S$ is separable and complete and a weak-convergence metric with measurable conditional distances is supplied, the conclusion is also conditional weak convergence in probability in the sense of [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]]. Under the null, the sampling law of $\Psi(L_MU_M)$ has the same limit. The maps may be squared norms, integrated linear contrasts, or any other continuous statistic of this scaled contrast.

$$\bar Y_i=\frac1{n_i}\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}Y_{i,t},\qquad \bar Y_P=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^K n_i\bar Y_i,\qquad R_{i,t}=Y_{i,t}-\bar Y_i.$$

$$c_{i,r}=\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j=1}^{N_i}A_{i,j,r}.$$

$$Y^*_{i,(s-1)b_i+r}=\bar Y_P+A_{i,J_{i,s},r}-c_{i,r}.$$

Write $\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)$ for its conditional Borel probability law given $\mathcal D_n$. For a fixed Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $E$, we say that $Z_n^*$ converges conditionally weakly in probability to $\mu$ when

$$d_w\!\left(\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*),\mu\right)\longrightarrow 0\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$

The metric is supplied as a hypothesis; this definition makes no metric-existence assertion. It applies to separable complete metric spaces, including separable Banach spaces, their closed linear subspaces and finite products.

Let S,T be metric spaces, $g:S\to T$ measurable, and $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$. If the discontinuity set $D_g$ is $\mu$-null, then $g_*\mu_n\Rightarrow g_*\mu$. Consequently $X_n\Rightarrow X$ implies $g(X_n)\Rightarrow g(X)$ whenever $P_X(D_g)=0$.

$X_n\to X$ in probability if and only if every subsequence of $(X_n)$ has a
further subsequence converging almost surely to $X$.

For Borel probabilities $\mu_n,\mu$ on a metric space S, the following are equivalent: (i) $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$; (ii) integrals converge for all bounded uniformly continuous real tests; (iii) $\limsup_n\mu_n(F)\le\mu(F)$ for every closed F; (iv) $\liminf_n\mu_n(G)\ge\mu(G)$ for every open G; (v) $\mu_n(A)\to\mu(A)$ for every Borel A with $\mu(\partial A)=0$.

No completeness or coupling is required.

Let $(E_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a decreasing sequence of measurable sets for a measure $\mu$. If $\mu(E_{n_0})<+\infty$ for some $n_0$, then

$$\mu\left(\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb N}E_n\right)=\inf_{n\in\mathbb N}\mu(E_n).$$

## Statement

Assume AC and all the process and weight hypotheses of [[lem-weighted-overlapping-block-moment-and-covariance-limits]], including squared normalization and convergence of each fixed-lag weight autocorrelation to one. Let $b=b_n\to\infty$ with $b/\sqrt n\to0$, $N=n-b+1$, $k=\lfloor n/b\rfloor$, $r=n-kb$, and

$$B_{j,q}=\sum_{\ell=1}^q c_{b,\ell}X_{j+\ell-1},\qquad \bar B_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NB_{j,q},\qquad C_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N(B_{j,q}-\bar B_q)\otimes(B_{j,q}-\bar B_q),$$

with $B_{j,0}=\bar B_0=C_0=0$. Conditional on the observations choose independent uniform starts $J_1,\ldots,J_{k+1}$ in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and set

$$Z_n^*=n^{-1/2}\left\{\sum_{s=1}^k(B_{J_s,b}-\bar B_b)+(B_{J_{k+1},r}-\bar B_r)\right\}.$$

Then, for the centered Hilbert Gaussian $G$ of covariance $\Gamma$,

$$\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)\Rightarrow\mathcal L(G)\quad\hbox{in probability},\qquad \left\|\operatorname{Cov}^*(Z_n^*)-\Gamma\right\|_1\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$

Trace-norm convergence implies convergence in Hilbert-Schmidt norm as well. The conditional laws are tight in probability: for every $\varepsilon,\eta>0$ there is a deterministic compact $K\subset H$ such that $\limsup_nP\{P^*(Z_n^*\notin K)>\varepsilon\}<\eta$. The complete blocks satisfy conditional Lindeberg, and the final partial block has $E E^*\|n^{-1/2}(B_{J_{k+1},r}-\bar B_r)\|^2=O(b/n)$. Replacing every $X_t$ by $X_t-M_n$ for any common data-dependent $M_n\in H$ leaves $Z_n^*$ and all its conditional covariances unchanged.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The assumptions and the conditional uniform-start randomization of the Statement. Write $\|\cdot\|_1$ for trace norm.

[F1] [[lem-weighted-overlapping-block-moment-and-covariance-limits]] supplies uniform integrability of $\|b^{-1/2}B_{1,b}\|^2$, $C_b/b\to\Gamma$ in trace norm in probability, $E\|\bar B_b/\sqrt b\|^2=O(b/N)$, and $E\|B_{1,q}\|^2\le Dq$ uniformly for $q\le b$. For any complete orthonormal basis and its projections $P_d$, putting $R_d=I-P_d$, it also supplies $E\|R_dB_{1,q}\|^2\le qD_d$ with $D_d\to0$.

[F2] [[thm-hilbert-valued-clt-for-l2-m-approximable-bernoulli-shifts]] supplies $G$ with positive trace-class covariance $\Gamma$. Under AC choose a complete eigenbasis for $\Gamma$ by [[cor-orthonormal-eigenbasis-for-a-compact-self-adjoint-operator]]. Thus $E\|R_dG\|^2=\operatorname{tr}(R_d\Gamma R_d)\to0$. AC is used for these inherited Hilbert-space constructions, not for an additional uncountable randomization.

[F3] [[lem-second-order-characteristic-function-expansion]] gives $|e^{iu}-1-iu+u^2/2|\le\min(|u|^3/3,4u^2)$. A centered normal of variance $v\ge0$ has characteristic function $e^{-t^2v/2}$ by [[lem-characteristic-function-of-a-normal-law]]. The characteristic-function criterion and Cramer--Wold apply also to degenerate limits ([[cor-characteristic-function-criterion-for-weak-convergence]], [[thm-cramer-wold-device]]).

[F4] A scalar sequence converges in probability exactly when every subsequence has an almost-surely convergent further subsequence ([[thm-subsequence-characterization-of-convergence-in-probability]], [[thm-almost-sure-subsequence-from-convergence-in-probability]]). Weak convergence on a metric space is equivalent to convergence against all bounded uniformly continuous tests by [[thm-portmanteau-theorem]]. Under the assumed AC, [[thm-levy-prokhorov-metric-metrizes-weak-convergence]] supplies the Levy-Prokhorov metric generating weak convergence on the separable Hilbert space $H$. Use this metric in [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]]. For each $n$ the conditional law is a finite mixture with deterministic probabilities and Borel data-dependent atoms: finite independent starts have only finitely many configurations. The map from its atom tuple to this law is continuous for weak convergence (test each bounded continuous function), hence its metric distance to the fixed law is a Borel data function.

[F5] Markov's inequality is [[cor-markov-inequality-for-random-variables]]. The trace-class ideal estimate is [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]], and [[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]] identifies the trace norm with the infimum of nuclear sums. The Hilbert-Schmidt norm is the basis square-sum in [[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]; [[lem-finite-bessel-inequality]] bounds finite sums of squared coordinates. These give the operator bounds proved in step 1.1.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is assumed as in [F2].

## Proof

**Given:** The stated process, weights, data and independent conditional block starts.

1.1 First, for a nuclear representation $T=\sum_j\langle\cdot,u_j\rangle v_j$ and an orthogonal projection $R$, its absolutely convergent trace has $|\operatorname{tr}(RTR)|\le\sum_j\|u_j\|\|v_j\|$. For every finite orthonormal set $E$, Minkowski and Bessel give $(\sum_{e\in E}\|Te\|^2)^{1/2}\le\sum_j\|v_j\|(\sum_{e\in E}|\langle e,u_j\rangle|^2)^{1/2}\le\sum_j\|u_j\|\|v_j\|$. Infinite nuclear sums follow from their summable tails. Taking the nuclear infimum proves $|\operatorname{tr}(RTR)|\le\|T\|_1$ and $\|T\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\|T\|_1$ by [F5]. Subtraction of $M_n$ replaces $B_{j,q}$ by $B_{j,q}-s_qM_n$, where $s_q=\sum_{\ell=1}^qc_{b,\ell}$ does not depend on $j$. It changes $\bar B_q$ by exactly the same amount. Thus every centered block is unchanged. Independence of the starts gives $\operatorname{Cov}^*(Z_n^*)=(kC_b+C_r)/n$. Positivity and the rank-one trace formula give $E\operatorname{tr}C_r\le E\|B_{1,r}\|^2\le Dr$, so $E\|C_r/n\|_1\le Db/n\to0$. Since $kb/n\to1$, [F1] now gives the asserted trace-norm covariance limit. The conditional squared norm of the centered remainder has expectation $\operatorname{tr}(C_r/n)$ and therefore its unconditional expectation tends to zero at rate $O(b/n)$. [given, F1, F5, algebra]

2.1 Set $U_j=B_{j,b}/\sqrt b$, $\bar U=\bar B_b/\sqrt b$, and $V_j=U_j-\bar U$. For any vectors $x,y$ and $a>0$, splitting according as the larger summand exceeds $a/2$ gives $\|x+y\|^2\mathbf1_{\{\|x+y\|>a\}}\le4\|x\|^2\mathbf1_{\{\|x\|>a/2\}}+4\|y\|^2\mathbf1_{\{\|y\|>a/2\}}$. Consequently, for each $\varepsilon>0$, the conditional Lindeberg sum of the $k$ complete blocks is at most
$$L_n(\varepsilon)=\frac{kb}{nN}\sum_{j=1}^N\|V_j\|^2\mathbf1_{\{\|V_j\|>\varepsilon\sqrt{n/b}\}},\qquad E L_n(\varepsilon)\le4E\!\left[\|U_1\|^2\mathbf1_{\{\|U_1\|>(\varepsilon/2)\sqrt{n/b}\}}\right]+4E\|\bar U\|^2\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $n/b\to\infty$, stationarity makes the expected empirical uncentered tail equal to that of $U_1$, and [F1] supplies uniform integrability and $E\|\bar U\|^2\to0$. Hence $L_n(\varepsilon)\to0$ in probability by [F5]. [F1, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Take any subsequence. Apply [F4] diagonally to the scalar trace-norm covariance error, $\operatorname{tr}(C_r/n)$, and $L_n(1/j)$ for positive integers $j$. There is a further subsequence on which all tend to zero almost surely. Fix a data outcome in this probability-one event. For any $a\in H$, let $\xi_n=\langle a,B_{J_1,b}-\bar B_b\rangle/\sqrt n$ and $v_n=kE^*\xi_n^2$. Step 1.1 and remainder negligibility give $v_n\to\langle\Gamma a,a\rangle$, and the norm Lindeberg bounds imply $kE^*[\xi_n^2\mathbf1_{\{|\xi_n|>\rho\}}]\to0$ for every $\rho>0$. The Taylor bound in [F3], split at $\rho$, gives
$$k\left|E^*e^{i\xi_n}-1+\tfrac12E^*\xi_n^2\right|\le (\rho/3)v_n+4kE^*[\xi_n^2\mathbf1_{\{|\xi_n|>\rho\}}].$$

manifest_row.statement:
Assume AC and all the process and weight hypotheses of [[lem-weighted-overlapping-block-moment-and-covariance-limits]], including squared normalization and convergence of each fixed-lag weight autocorrelation to one. Let $b=b_n\to\infty$ with $b/\sqrt n\to0$, $N=n-b+1$, $k=\lfloor n/b\rfloor$, $r=n-kb$, and

$$B_{j,q}=\sum_{\ell=1}^q c_{b,\ell}X_{j+\ell-1},\qquad \bar B_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NB_{j,q},\qquad C_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N(B_{j,q}-\bar B_q)\otimes(B_{j,q}-\bar B_q),$$

with $B_{j,0}=\bar B_0=C_0=0$. Conditional on the observations choose independent uniform starts $J_1,\ldots,J_{k+1}$ in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and set

$$Z_n^*=n^{-1/2}\left\{\sum_{s=1}^k(B_{J_s,b}-\bar B_b)+(B_{J_{k+1},r}-\bar B_r)\right\}.$$

Then, for the centered Hilbert Gaussian $G$ of covariance $\Gamma$,

$$\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)\Rightarrow\mathcal L(G)\quad\hbox{in probability},\qquad \left\|\operatorname{Cov}^*(Z_n^*)-\Gamma\right\|_1\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$

Trace-norm convergence implies convergence in Hilbert-Schmidt norm as well. The conditional laws are tight in probability: for every $\varepsilon,\eta>0$ there is a deterministic compact $K\subset H$ such that $\limsup_nP\{P^*(Z_n^*\notin K)>\varepsilon\}<\eta$. The complete blocks satisfy conditional Lindeberg, and the final partial block has $E E^*\|n^{-1/2}(B_{J_{k+1},r}-\bar B_r)\|^2=O(b/n)$. Replacing every $X_t$ by $X_t-M_n$ for any common data-dependent $M_n\in H$ leaves $Z_n^*$ and all its conditional covariances unchanged.

be Hilbert spaces over the same real or complex scalar field and let $T\in\mathcal B(H,K)$ be compact
([[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Then $T$ is trace class
([[def-trace-class-operator]]) if and only if there are families
$(u_j)_{j\ge1}$ in $H$ and $(v_j)_{j\ge1}$ in $K$, indexed by the positive
integers, with
$$\sum_{j\ge1}\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<+\infty$$
such that the zero-based sequence of finite-rank operators defined by $R_0=0$
and
$$R_m:=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\langle\cdot,u_j\rangle v_j\qquad(m\ge1)$$
converges to $T$ in operator norm ([[def-operator-norm]],
[[def-metric-convergence]]).  Here the displayed scalar series is, under the
library convention, the series of the sequence
$(\|u_{m+1}\|\,\|v_{m+1}\|)_{m\in\mathbb N}$. In that case
$$\|T\|_1=\inf\Bigl\{\sum_{j\ge1}\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|:\ R_m\to T\ \text{in operator norm}\Bigr\},$$
the infimum being over all such **nuclear representations** of $T$, with the
same zero-based shift understood in every displayed sum, and the
infimum is attained: using its positive-integer index set and padding finite rank by zeros,
the singular-value series
$T=\sum_{j\in J}s_j\langle\cdot,e_j\rangle f_j$ is a nuclear representation with
sum $\|T\|_1$.

Throughout, $H$ and $K$ are real or complex Hilbert spaces with the pairing
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-hilbert-space]]), $T\in\mathcal B(H,K)$ is a bounded linear operator
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]) of
operator norm $\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]), and $E$ is a **Hilbert basis**
of $H$, that is, a complete orthonormal subset of $H$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
The basis $E$ is **supplied as data**; the definitions below are stated
relative to it.

**The Hilbert–Schmidt square-sum.** The family $(\|Te\|^2)_{e\in E}$ consists of
nonnegative real numbers and is indexed by the arbitrary set $E$. Its sum is the
supremum of the finite subsums,

$$s_E(T):=\sum_{e\in E}\|Te\|^2:=\sup\Bigl\{\sum_{e\in F}\|Te\|^2 \;:\; F\subseteq E \text{ finite}\Bigr\}\in[0,+\infty],$$

in the finite-subset-supremum convention of
[[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]; the empty finite
subset contributes the empty sum $0$, so the supremum is over a nonempty
set and exists in $[0,+\infty]$. No enumeration, ordering or countability of
$E$ is used or asserted, and no choice is performed: the supremum ranges over
the set of finite subsets of the fixed index set $E$. For finite $E$ the
supremum is the ordinary finite sum over $E$, because all terms are
nonnegative.

**Hilbert–Schmidt relative to a basis.** The operator $T$ is
**Hilbert–Schmidt relative to $E$** when $s_E(T)<+\infty$, that is, when the
finite subsums are bounded above in $\mathbb R$. In that case the
**Hilbert–Schmidt norm of $T$ relative to $E$** is the nonnegative square root

$$\|T\|_{HS,E}:=\Bigl(\sum_{e\in E}\|Te\|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\in[0,+\infty).$$

When $s_E(T)=+\infty$, no Hilbert–Schmidt norm relative to $E$ is defined, and
$T$ is not Hilbert–Schmidt relative to $E$.

**Degenerate and extreme cases.** The zero operator satisfies $s_E(0)=0$ for
every basis $E$, so it is Hilbert–Schmidt relative to every basis with norm
$0$. If $H=\{0\}$ then the empty family is a Hilbert basis of $H$, the only
finite subset is empty, and $s_\varnothing(T)=0$ for the only linear operator
$T:\{0\}\to K$; that operator is Hilbert–Schmidt relative to the empty basis
with norm $0$. If $H$ is finite dimensional and $E$ is finite, $s_E(T)$ is an
ordinary finite sum of the squared norms $\|Te\|^2$, and $T$ is automatically
Hilbert–Schmidt relative to $E$.

**The basis is part of the notation.** The symbol $\|T\|_{HS,E}$ keeps the
basis in the subscript on purpose. Until the next result is proved, the phrase
"$T$ is Hilbert–Schmidt" is never used without a specified Hilbert basis, and
nothing here asserts that a Hilbert basis of $H$ exists: the existence of $E$
is a hypothesis of the definition, and the question of whether the finiteness
of $s_E(T)$ and the value $\|T\|_{HS,E}$ depend on $E$ is taken up in
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. In particular this
definition makes no basis-existence claim and no comparison with the operator
norm $\|T\|$; every such statement is proved later, where its own hypotheses
are displayed.

**Notation.** For a finite $F\subseteq E$ we write
$s_F(T):=\sum_{e\in F}\|Te\|^2$ for the finite subsum, so that
$s_E(T)=\sup\{s_F(T):F\subseteq E \text{ finite}\}$.

Let $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ be an orthonormal family in a real or complex inner-product
space $H$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
let $F\subseteq I$ be finite, and for $x\in H$ put

$$P_Fx:=\sum_{i\in F}\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i .$$Then: 1. $P_Fx$ lies in the span of $\{e_i : i\in F\}$, and $\|P_Fx\|^2=\sum_{i\in F}|\langle x,e_i\rangle|^2$; 2. the residual $x-P_Fx$ is orthogonal to every $e_j$ with $j\in F$, hence to every vector of the span of $\{e_i : i\in F\}$; 3. $\|x-P_Fx\|^2=\|x\|^2-\sum_{i\in F}|\langle x,e_i\rangle|^2$, and therefore the **finite Bessel inequality** holds:$$\sum_{i\in F}|\langle x,e_i\rangle|^2\le\|x\|^2 ;$$4. $P_Fx$ is the unique best approximation to $x$ from the span of $\{e_i : i\in F\}$: for every $y$ in that span,$$\|x-y\|^2=\|x-P_Fx\|^2+\|P_Fx-y\|^2\ge\|x-P_Fx\|^2 ,$$
   with equality if and only if $y=P_Fx$.

At $F=\varnothing$ the sum defining $P_Fx$ is empty, so $P_Fx=0$ and the
identities read $\|x\|^2=\|x\|^2$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

## Statement

Use the actual independent-tail replacement construction of [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]], and put $X=X_0$, $\mathcal F_m=\sigma(\delta_0,\ldots,\delta_{-m+1})$ and $\delta_m=(\mathbb E\|X-X_{0,m}\|_H^2)^{1/2}$. There is an $\mathcal F_m$-measurable square-integrable conditional mean $g_m$ such that
$$\delta_m^2=2\mathbb E\|X-g_m\|_H^2.$$
The conditional mean minimizes $\mathbb E\|X-Y\|_H^2$ over all square-integrable $\mathcal F_m$-measurable $H$-valued $Y$. Consequently $\delta_{m+1}\le\delta_m$ for every $m\ge1$, and
$$\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_m<\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad m\delta_m\longrightarrow0.$$
In particular no process under this replacement definition has summable replacement errors while failing the displayed rate condition.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The separable real Hilbert space, supplied mutually independent original and replacement innovations, measurable filter, and finite second moment in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]] supplies the measurable filter, separable complete Hilbert target, independent tail arrays and their matching product laws.

[F2] [[thm-independent-random-elements-have-product-joint-law]] and [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] identify the joint law of independent prefix and tail variables with its product and permit nonnegative section integrals.

[F3] [[thm-dominated-convergence]], [[thm-fatou-lemma]] and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-for-random-variables]] give the scalar dominated limits, lower integral bound and square-integrable product estimates below.

[F4] [[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]] gives the null-union rule. The Hilbert norm and inner product obey the finite Pythagorean identity and Cauchy–Schwarz by [F1].

## Proof

1.1 Fix $m$. Write the innovation input as $(A,B)$, with $A$ its first $m$ coordinates and $B$ its remaining tail. Its law is a product by [F2]. The replacement uses $(A,B')$, where $B,B'$ have the same tail law and are independent of one another and of $A$. To construct the conditional mean without assuming a vector conditional-expectation theorem, take finite-valued measurable approximants $f_j(A,B)$ to the filter $f(A,B)$ with $\|f_j-f\|_{L^2(H)}\le2^{-2j}$. They exist explicitly: include zero in a fixed dense sequence in $H$, use the first nearest point among its first $N$ points, and let $N$ increase. The error is at most $\|f\|$ and tends pointwise to zero, so [F3] gives $L^2$ convergence; choose the first $N$ achieving the indicated bound. For each finite-valued $f_j$, its tail average $g_j(A)=\int f_j(A,b)\,\nu_{\rm tail}(db)$ is a finite linear combination of measurable section probabilities, hence is measurable by [F2]. Convexity of the squared Hilbert norm for finite averages, extended by simple scalar integration, gives $\mathbb E\|g_j-g_k\|^2\le\mathbb E\|f_j-f_k\|^2$. [F1, F2, F3, given, construct]

1.2 The last inequality implies $\sum_j\mathbb E\|g_{j+1}-g_j\|<\infty$, by [F3] and the chosen error bounds. Tonelli [F2] makes the sum of these norms finite almost surely. Completeness of $H$ gives a measurable pointwise limit $g_m$, set to zero on the null complement. Fatou [F3], applied to $\|g_j-g_k\|^2$ as $k\to\infty$, gives $g_j\to g_m$ in $L^2(H)$. In particular $g_m$ is square integrable. For finite-valued $\mathcal F_m$-measurable $Y$, finite sums and the section-integral identity give $\mathbb E\langle f_j(A,B),Y\rangle=\mathbb E\langle g_j(A),Y\rangle$. Pass to the limit by Cauchy–Schwarz. Approximate any square-integrable $\mathcal F_m$-measurable $Y$ by its finite nearest-point approximants as in step 1.1, and pass to the limit again. Thus $\mathbb E\langle X-g_m,Y\rangle=0$ for every such $Y$, which is the conditional-mean identity and implies
$$\mathbb E\|X-Y\|^2=\mathbb E\|X-g_m\|^2+\mathbb E\|g_m-Y\|^2.$$
This proves the stated minimization, without a regular conditional law on the innovation space. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.1 Conditional product integration for the two copies of the finite-valued $f_j$ gives $\mathbb E\langle f_j(A,B),f_j(A,B')\rangle=\mathbb E\|g_j(A)\|^2$. Passing to the $L^2$ limits by [F3] gives $\mathbb E\langle X,X_{0,m}\rangle=\mathbb E\|g_m\|^2$. The two copies have the same second moment by [F1]. Expanding their squared difference therefore yields $\delta_m^2=2(\mathbb E\|X\|^2-\mathbb E\|g_m\|^2)=2\mathbb E\|X-g_m\|^2$, the final equality also following from step 1.2 with $Y=g_m$. The sigma-fields increase with $m$, so every $\mathcal F_m$-measurable competitor is an $\mathcal F_{m+1}$-measurable competitor. The minimum residual squared norm cannot increase; hence $\delta_{m+1}\le\delta_m$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 For $m\ge2$, monotonicity gives $\lfloor m/2\rfloor\delta_m\le\sum_{j=\lceil m/2\rceil}^{m}\delta_j$. If the full nonnegative series is summable, its right-hand tail tends to zero. Since $m/\lfloor m/2\rfloor\le3$, this implies $m\delta_m\to0$. Thus the rate-separation example requested in the former design cannot exist under the actual independent-tail replacement convention. This is a proved implication, not an absence of a known counterexample. [step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎

Let $\mathcal B$ be the Borel sigma-algebra of $[0,1]$, generated by intervals with rational endpoints; let $dt$ be Lebesgue measure restricted to $\mathcal B$, and set $H=L^2([0,1],\mathcal B,dt;\mathbb R)$, with inner product $\langle x,y\rangle_H=\int_0^1x(u)y(u)\,du$. We use the quotient-by-null-functions convention for $L^2$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). The measure space is finite and countably generated, so under Countable Choice $H$ is separable ([[thm-l-p-of-a-sigma-finite-countably-generated-measure-space-is-separable]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-separable-space]]); [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]] verifies that this real pairing makes the quotient a Hilbert space.

Let $(S,\mathcal S,\nu)$ be a probability space and $(\delta_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ an independent identically distributed family of $S$-valued random elements with law $\nu$ ([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]], [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]], [[def-independent-random-elements]]). A **causal Bernoulli shift** with innovation law $\nu$ is a process
$$X_t=f(\delta_t,\delta_{t-1},\delta_{t-2},\ldots),\qquad t\in\mathbb Z,$$
where $f:S^{\mathbb N_0}\to H$ is measurable from the product sigma-algebra $\mathcal S^{\otimes\mathbb N_0}$ to the Borel sigma-algebra of $H$. This product-measurability formulation is meaningful for a merely measurable innovation space $S$.

On an independent product extension, take replacement innovations $\delta'_{t,m,k}$, indexed by $t\in\mathbb Z$, $m\in\mathbb N_0$, and integers $k\le t-m$, all with law $\nu$, mutually independent, and independent of the original innovations. Such a countable family and its product with the original probability space exist under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[cor-countable-independent-copies-exist]], [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]]). For $m\ge1$ define
$$X_{t,m}=f(\delta_t,\ldots,\delta_{t-m+1},\delta'_{t,m,t-m},\delta'_{t,m,t-m-1},\ldots),$$
and define the full replacement $X_{t,0}=f(\delta'_{t,0,t},\delta'_{t,0,t-1},\ldots)$. Each $X_{t,m}$ has the same marginal law as $X_t$; for fixed $m\ge1$ the sequence $(X_{t,m})_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is strictly stationary and $m$-dependent because its original-innovation windows have length $m$ and its replacement arrays are independent across $t$.

For every fixed $m\ge0$, the joint process $(X_t,X_{t,m})_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is strictly stationary: shifting all indices relabels a family of mutually independent innovations with the same law and commutes with the defining measurable maps. Consequently $D_{t,m}:=X_t-X_{t,m}$ is stationary and $\|D_{t,m}\|_{L^2(H)}=\delta_m$ for every $t$.

Write $\|X\|_{L^2(H)}=(\mathbb E\|X\|_H^2)^{1/2}$ and
$$\delta_m=\|X_0-X_{0,m}\|_{L^2(H)},\qquad m\ge0.$$
The process is **$L^2$-$m$-approximable** when
$$\mathbb E\|X_0\|_H^2<\infty\qquad\hbox{and}\qquad\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_m<\infty.$$
The same marginal law gives $\delta_0\le2\|X_0\|_{L^2(H)}<\infty$. For a Bochner-integrable $H$-valued random element $Y$, write $\mathbb E_B Y=\int Y\,d\mathbb P$; the moment condition makes $X_t$ and every $X_{t,m}$ Bochner integrable ([[def-bochner-integrable-function]], [[thm-bochner-integrability-criterion]]).

Here **strict stationarity** means invariance of every finite-dimensional law under integer shifts. A process is **$m$-dependent** if, for every $a\in\mathbb Z$, the sigma-algebras generated by $(X_s)_{s\le a}$ and $(X_s)_{s\ge a+m+1}$ are independent ([[def-independent-sigma-algebras-and-events]]). The stated input windows for $X_{t,m}$ are disjoint across these two index ranges, so they satisfy this definition.

Let $n\ge1$, and let
$X_i:(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\to(S_i,\Sigma_i)$ for $i<n$ be independent
random elements. Define

$$X=(X_0,\dots,X_{n-1}):\Omega\to\prod_{i<n}S_i.$$

Then $X$ is a random element of
$\left(\prod_{i<n}S_i,\bigotimes_{i<n}\Sigma_i\right)$, and its law is the
finite product of the marginal laws:

$$\mathbb P_X=\bigotimes_{i<n}\mathbb P_{X_i}.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

Let $(f_n)$ be nonnegative measurable functions. Then
$$\int \liminf_{n\to\infty}f_n\,d\mu\le\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int f_n\,d\mu.$$

If $X,Y\in L^2(\mathbb P)$ are real random variables, then
$$\mathbb E[|XY|]\le\big(\mathbb E[X^2]\big)^{1/2}\big(\mathbb E[Y^2]\big)^{1/2}.$$

Equality holds if and only if at least one of $X,Y$ is zero almost surely, or
there is a constant $c>0$ with
$$|X|^2=c\,|Y|^2\qquad\mathbb P\text{-almost surely}.$$

Let $\mu$ be a measure and let $(E_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$ be measurable. Then

$$\mu\left(\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb N}E_k\right)\le\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\mu(E_k).$$

For every $m\in\mathbb N$ one also has

$$\mu\left(\bigcup_{k<m}E_k\right)\le\sum_{k<m}\mu(E_k),$$

including $m=0$, where both sides are $0$.

## Summary

This page defines overlapping moving blocks and tapered blocks for Hilbert-valued time series, proves their finite-sample conditional covariance identities, and verifies the taper normalization. It also proves that position-centered block resampling gives every bootstrap series the same pooled conditional mean, and gives a conditional K-sample limit theorem for continuous statistics and Hadamard-differentiable maps. The MBB and TBB sample-mean CLTs are proved with the displayed source rate, block-length regime, AC assumption inherited from the sampling CLT, covariance target and topology. Under the assigned independent-tail replacement convention, [[lem-independent-tail-replacement-errors-are-monotone]] proves that replacement errors are nonincreasing and summability already implies the displayed rate $m\delta_m\to0$; this condition does not define a stronger process class here. Two shared weighted-block lemmas establish empirical covariance consistency in trace norm, conditional Lindeberg, Hilbert-space tightness and negligibility of the final partial block for arbitrary sample sizes. The covariance conclusions therefore hold in Hilbert-Schmidt norm as well. This page makes no path-process FCLT claim.
