**Input:** a fixed number $K\ge2$ of observed series $Y_{i,1},\ldots,Y_{i,n_i}$ in a real Hilbert space $H$, positive integer sample sizes $n_i$, total size $M=\sum_{i=1}^K n_i$, integer block lengths $1\le b_i\le n_i$, and a mode, moving or tapered. For tapered mode also supply an admissible window with positive block norm at each $b_i$. Put

$$\bar Y_i=\frac1{n_i}\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}Y_{i,t},\qquad \bar Y_P=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^K n_i\bar Y_i,\qquad R_{i,t}=Y_{i,t}-\bar Y_i.$$

For each series $i=1,\ldots,K$, let $N_i=n_i-b_i+1$ and $k_i=\lceil n_i/b_i\rceil$. For every candidate start $j=1,\ldots,N_i$ and position $r=1,\ldots,b_i$, define the following arrays. In moving mode set $A_{i,j,r}=R_{i,j+r-1}$. In tapered mode set $A_{i,j,r}=a_{b_i}w_{b_i}(r)R_{i,j+r-1}$, with $a_{b_i}$ and $w_{b_i}$ as in [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]]. For each $i=1,\ldots,K$ and $s=1,\ldots,k_i$, draw independent uniform starts $J_{i,s}\in\{1,\ldots,N_i\}$, using the index law of [[alg-overlapping-block-resampling]]. For each within-block position define

$$c_{i,r}=\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j=1}^{N_i}A_{i,j,r}.$$

**Output:** for each $i$, a pseudo-series $Y^*_{i,1},\ldots,Y^*_{i,n_i}$. In the order $s=1,\ldots,k_i$, retain the positions $r=1,\ldots,q_{i,s}$, where $q_{i,s}=\min\{b_i,n_i-(s-1)b_i\}$, and set

$$Y^*_{i,(s-1)b_i+r}=\bar Y_P+A_{i,J_{i,s},r}-c_{i,r}.$$

Thus a divisible sample uses $k_i$ complete blocks; otherwise only the first $n_i-b_i\lfloor n_i/b_i\rfloor$ positions of the final block are retained. This centers each resampled residual position by its own conditional average, then gives every pseudo-series the same pooled location $\bar Y_P$. All block starts are conditionally independent across blocks and across series.

For fixed data and either mode of [[alg-k-sample-null-constrained-block-bootstrap]], every pseudo-observation in every series has conditional expectation $\bar Y_P$. Consequently, for each $i$,

$$E^*\bar Y_i^*=\bar Y_P,$$

so the conditional mean functions of the $K$ pseudo-series are equal.

Let $E$ be a separable complete metric space, let $\mathcal D_n$ be the sigma-algebra generated by the observed data at sample size $n$, and let $Z_n^*$ be a bootstrap random element whose remaining randomness is the resampling randomization. Write $\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)$ for its conditional Borel probability law given $\mathcal D_n$. Supply as part of the data a metric $d_w$ on Borel probability measures on $E$ such that $d_w(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$ exactly when $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$ in the sense of [[def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures]]. Assume the displayed metric distance is a measurable real random variable. For a fixed Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $E$, we say that $Z_n^*$ converges conditionally weakly in probability to $\mu$ when

$$d_w\!\left(\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*),\mu\right)\longrightarrow 0\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$

The metric is supplied as a hypothesis; this definition makes no metric-existence assertion. It applies to separable complete metric spaces, including separable Banach spaces, their closed linear subspaces and finite products.

Let S,T be metric spaces, $g:S\to T$ measurable, and $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$. If the discontinuity set $D_g$ is $\mu$-null, then $g_*\mu_n\Rightarrow g_*\mu$. Consequently $X_n\Rightarrow X$ implies $g(X_n)\Rightarrow g(X)$ whenever $P_X(D_g)=0$.

$X_n\to X$ in probability if and only if every subsequence of $(X_n)$ has a
further subsequence converging almost surely to $X$.

For Borel probabilities $\mu_n,\mu$ on a metric space S, the following are equivalent: (i) $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$; (ii) integrals converge for all bounded uniformly continuous real tests; (iii) $\limsup_n\mu_n(F)\le\mu(F)$ for every closed F; (iv) $\liminf_n\mu_n(G)\ge\mu(G)$ for every open G; (v) $\mu_n(A)\to\mu(A)$ for every Borel A with $\mu(\partial A)=0$.

For Borel probability measures $\mu_n,\mu$ on a metric space S, write $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$ if $\int f\,d\mu_n\to\int f\,d\mu$ for every bounded continuous real function f on S. Continuity is [[def-metric-continuity]]. Such f is Borel measurable (inverse images of open sets are open) and $\int|f|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\mu(S)<\infty$, so the integrals are finite in [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. No completeness or coupling is required.

Let $(E_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a decreasing sequence of measurable sets for a measure $\mu$. If $\mu(E_{n_0})<+\infty$ for some $n_0$, then

$$\mu\left(\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb N}E_n\right)=\inf_{n\in\mathbb N}\mu(E_n).$$

derivations.claim: Since every pseudo-series has conditional mean $\bar Y_P$ by [F1]-[F2], that common location cancels in every contrast. Direct substitution gives $L_MU_M^*=\bigl(\sqrt M(\bar Y_i^*-\bar Y_K^*)\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1}$ and $L_MU_M=\bigl(\sqrt M(\bar Y_i-\bar Y_K)\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1}$. Thus the two statistics use the same contrast map; under the null the common population mean also cancels from $L_MU_M$.

Endow the finite products with their Hilbert product norms. The coefficients in $L_M$ converge to those of $L_\theta$, hence $a_M=\|L_M-L_\theta\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0$. For $R>0$, the function $\chi_R(z)=\min\{1,\max\{0,\|z\|-R\}\}$ is bounded and continuous, vanishes when $\|z\|\le R$, and equals one when $\|z\|\ge R+1$. Thus [F5] and the given weak convergence imply
$$\limsup_M\Pr(\|U_M\|\ge R+1)\le E\chi_R(G)\le\Pr(\|G\|>R)\longrightarrow0\quad(R\to\infty).$$
The last limit follows from continuity from above since $G$ has finite norm. Given $\delta>0$, eventually $a_M(R+1)\le\delta$, so $\Pr(\|(L_M-L_\theta)U_M\|>\delta)\le\Pr(\|U_M\|>R+1)$. First take the limit superior in $M$ and then let $R\to\infty$. Hence $(L_M-L_\theta)U_M\to0$ in probability, without a compact-tightness or AC premise. For the conditional discrepancy, every supplied compact $C\subset H^K$ is norm bounded, say by $R_C$. For arbitrary $\epsilon,\eta>0$, conditional tightness supplies such a $C$ with $\limsup_M\Pr\{\Pr^*(U_M^*\notin C)>\epsilon\}<\eta$. Eventually $a_MR_C\le\delta$, so $\Pr^*(\|(L_M-L_\theta)U_M^*\|>\delta)\le\Pr^*(U_M^*\notin C)$. Since $\eta$ is arbitrary, each conditional discrepancy probability tends to zero in probability.

By [F4], $L_\theta U_M\Rightarrow L_\theta G$. For a closed $B\subset H^{K-1}$, the sampling probability of $L_MU_M\in B$ is at most the discrepancy probability from step 2.1 plus $\Pr(L_\theta U_M\in B^\delta)$, where $B^\delta$ is the closed $\delta$-neighbourhood. Apply [F6] and let $\delta\downarrow0$ to obtain $L_MU_M\Rightarrow L_\theta G$. For the conditional version, combine the input weak-metric distance, truncated at one, with the weighted sum $\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j}\Pr^*(\|(L_M-L_\theta)U_M^*\|>1/j)$. This scalar tends to zero in probability by truncation of the geometric tail and step 2.1. Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence on which it tends to zero almost surely by [F6]. On each such outcome, [F4] gives weak convergence of the fixed-map conditional laws, and the same closed-neighbourhood inequality proves weak convergence of the varying-map conditional laws to $\mathcal L(L_\theta G)$.

Apply [F4] to $\Psi$ for the sampling convergence and, on every almost-sure subsequence outcome of step 2.2, for conditional convergence. Every bounded continuous $f:S\to\mathbb R$ then has convergent conditional expectations on those outcomes; [F6] gives their convergence in probability along the whole sequence. This proves the stated testwise conclusion for arbitrary metric $S$. When the supplied output weak-convergence metric is available on separable complete $S$, the same outcome-wise weak convergence says its distance to the fixed limiting law tends to zero. Applying [F6] to that measurable scalar distance proves the metric conditional conclusion as well.
